column6:
'Tab' means three things:

  Another full-screen thing (shell, server, logs)  ->  tmux WINDOW
      Alt-a c = new, Alt-1..9 = jump, Alt-n/Alt-p = next/prev, Alt-a , = rename
  Another file in the editor                      ->  Vim BUFFER (shown as the tab bar on top)
      Space Space = find a file, Tab / Q = next / prev, Space 1..9 = jump
  A second whole layout in the editor (rare)      ->  Vim TAB PAGE
      Space t n = new, Space t c = close, ]t [t = switch

Avoid terminal-app tabs for projects: they die with the terminal, tmux windows do not.

column3: What goes in the shell, tmux, or Vim?
column6:
Shell: running things. git, make, npm test, docker, ssh, cd, one-off commands.
tmux:  keeping things alive and side by side. One session per project, a server in
       window 2, logs in a pane, detach/reattach, ssh that survives a dropped connection.
Vim:   reading and changing code. Files, search, go-to-definition, blame, diffs, Claude.

Test: text I am editing -> Vim. Keeps running while I do other things -> tmux. A command -> shell.
They nest: shell inside tmux, Vim inside the shell.

column3: How do I start working on a project?
column6:
cd into the project, then run  t

It attaches to (or creates) a tmux session named after the directory. Then start the
editor with  vim .  and open a second window for a server or tests with  Alt-a c.

column3: How do I switch between projects?
column6: From inside tmux:  t other-project  (creates it if needed, switches without nesting)\nOr Alt-w to pick from a tree of every session and window. Alt-a s shows sessions only.

column3: How do I leave and come back later?
column6:
Just close the terminal, or press Alt-a d to detach. Everything keeps running.
Later: cd into the project and run  t  (or  tmux attach).

After a reboot sessions are gone. Before shutting down:  tmux-session save
afterwards:  tmux-session restore  (recreates sessions and windows, not pane layouts).

column3: How do I find a file or search the project?
column6:
In Vim:
  Space Space   fuzzy file finder (git aware)
  Space f g     search text in the whole project (ripgrep)
  Space f l     search lines in this file
  Space s       :Grep into the quickfix list
In the shell:  Ctrl-t (file picker), Alt-c (jump to a directory), z name (jump to a frequent dir),
  rg text  (search),  fd name  (find files).

column3: Who changed this line and why?
column6:
The dim text at the end of the cursor line is the inline blame (author, when, commit subject).

  Space g m   popup with the full commit and diff behind this line
  Space g L   every commit that touched this line
  Space g l   history of this file
  Space g b   full blame window (Enter opens a commit)
  Space g B   turn the inline text off / on

column3: How do I use Claude here?
column6:
Neovim: Space a c toggles Claude beside your code. It sees your file and selection;
        proposed edits show as diffs: Space a a accepts, Space a d denies.
Vim:    :Claude (or Space a c) opens the CLI in a split.
tmux:   Alt-a C opens Claude in a pane on the right.
Shell:  cc  (ccc continues the last conversation, ccr resumes one).

column3: How do I read a README rendered in the terminal?
column6:
Shell: md  (README.md here),  md FILE,  md -f  (pick a file with live preview)
tmux:  Alt-a m pops up the README over your work, Alt-a M lets you pick a file
Vim:   Space m p  or  :Md.  In Neovim markdown also renders in place; Space m r toggles.
Inside the pager: j/k scroll, / search, q quit.

column3: How do I copy and paste?
column6:
Vim: yanks go to the system clipboard automatically, so just paste anywhere.
tmux: drag with the mouse to select and copy, or Alt-a [ for copy mode, v to start,
      y to copy. It lands in the system clipboard (also over ssh).
Paste into Vim without overwriting what you yanked: select, then Space p.

column3: How do I scroll back in tmux?
column6: Use the mouse wheel, or Alt-a [ to enter copy mode (move with vim keys, Ctrl-u / Ctrl-d for pages,\n/ to search). Press q to leave.

Option is not acting as Alt. Fix it in your terminal:
  Ghostty    make terminal   (sets macos-option-as-alt)
  iTerm2     Profiles > Keys > Left Option key: Esc+
  Terminal   Settings > Profiles > Keyboard > Use Option as Meta key

column3: I am stuck in Vim. How do I quit?
column6: Esc first, then:\n  :w   save        :q   quit        :wq  save and quit\n  :q!  quit and throw changes away  :qa  quit everything   (Space q does :qa)

column3: How do I change these settings?
column6:
Shell:  v-rc (shell files)   v-vrc (vimrc)   v-tmux (tmux.conf), then  s-rc  to restart the shell
Vim:    edit, then  Space R  to reload
tmux:   edit, then  Alt-r  to reload
Machine-specific shell bits go in ~/.shellrc.local, Vim ones in ~/.vimrc.local.

column3: How do I update or repair the install?
column6:
From the env-settings directory (c-env):
  make doctor        which tools are installed
  make update        pull and update plugins
  make vim-plugins   (re)install Vim plugins
  make lsp           language servers for Neovim
  make               list everything
Fuzzy-search every key, command and how-to. Type to filter, Enter to read the full card.\nAlso: Alt-/ in the shell, Alt-a ? in tmux, Space ? in Vim.
